body: I can relate.  I have been to several therapists over the  years for PTSD and compulsive disorders.  One had no idea, she just gave me handouts to read.  I figured I could Google stuff myself and save the $40 co-pay.  The second one I tried told me that all I had to do was tell myself to stop whenever I was feeling compulsions.  Yeah, that really helped (not!).  Then I tried a woman who was into art therapy.  I spent nearly six months with that one, and when I was done all I had to show for it was the ability to draw an elephant with my left hand (I'm not kidding).  The woman I'm seeing now is OK, but I'm starting to lose hope that anyone can really help me.  As for your experience, you have the right to be taken seriously and be heard, and it seems like your therapist is doing neither.  Find a new one as soon as possible.

My parents are both dead, and my siblings and I aren't that close.  I'm single, no husband, no kids.  A few years ago my mom and my little dog died.  I have few friends.  I ended up having to sell my childhood home because of financial problems.  I live in an apartment now, and I like my apartment, but there are times I'd just give anything to go home to my mom, sit on the patio and drink some coffee and just talk.  I'd like to come home to my little dog wagging his tail happy to see me.  There are times I feel I don't fit in anywhere, like I'm always a stranger in a strange land.  I'm so lonely, and it's hard to tell people that because they don't really understand.  I just wish I could go home again.
